Unzc731iCUY.summary: Patrick Winston's long-running MIT lecture on public speaking teaches heuristic rules for talks. It covers how to start, use time and place, boards, props and slides, and how to inform, persuade and finish.
Unzc731iCUY.why: HN treats it as the canonical, near-universally recommended lecture on giving talks and presentations.

UzxYlbK2c7E.summary: The first lecture of Andrew Ng's Stanford CS229 Machine Learning course, giving an overview of the course. It introduces supervised and unsupervised learning, learning theory and reinforcement learning.
UzxYlbK2c7E.why: Recommended as the rigorous, math-heavy original course, deeper than the Coursera version, for learning machine learning.

Uhx-26GfCBU.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that winter is not what stops Canadians cycling, using Oulu, Finland as proof that safe, well-maintained cycling infrastructure enables year-round biking despite harsh weather.
Uhx-26GfCBU.why: HN links it whenever someone claims cold or snow rules out cycling, as the concise rebuttal that infrastructure and maintenance decide it.

UF8uR6Z6KLc.summary: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford commencement address, told through three stories: connecting the dots, love and loss, and death. It includes the calligraphy class and the 'stay hungry, stay foolish' close.
UF8uR6Z6KLc.why: HN returns to it for motivation and perspective, and quotes it constantly, especially the connect-the-dots and remembering-death passages.

UCgoxQCf5Jg.summary: Fredrik Knudsen's 86-minute documentary on Terry A. Davis, creator of TempleOS, tracing his work, his schizophrenia and his decline. It is a chronological video essay built on his public posts and videos.
UCgoxQCf5Jg.why: Regarded as the definitive, if heartbreaking, account of Terry Davis and TempleOS.

U7VwtOrwceo.summary: Microsoft's Tony Chen explains how the Xbox One was designed to resist physical attacks, including secure boot, encrypted memory, a security processor and a hypervisor. The goal was to make any hardware attack cost more than the price of many games.
U7VwtOrwceo.why: HN points to it constantly in console, DRM and hardware-security threads as the authoritative account of Xbox One's threat model.

Uj-rK8V-rik.summary: Chris Urmson's SXSW 2016 talk on Google's self-driving car project, covering 1.3 million self-driven miles and the gap between hype and reality. It shows sensor visualizations and playbacks of hard situations the cars met, and discusses failures such as the low-speed bus collision.
Uj-rK8V-rik.why: HN returns to it repeatedly as one of the best candid talks on how a real self-driving system sees the road and where it struggles.

Up7LcbGZFuo.summary: Scott Wlaschin's NDC talk on using statically typed functional programming, F# in particular, to model a business domain. Types are used to represent the domain precisely and to encode business rules so that illegal states cannot be built, with the compiler acting as an instant unit test.
Up7LcbGZFuo.why: HN people recommend it as an eye-opening talk whose domain-modeling ideas carry over to other languages and make a strong compiler feel like a coding partner.

US8QG9I1XW0.summary: Mark Seemann argues that functional programming naturally yields many of the best practices object-oriented developers learn painfully. He shows how functional architecture leads to a pit of success, with a pure core and impure shell.
US8QG9I1XW0.why: Recommended as a practical demonstration of how functional thinking improves design without going off the deep end.

Uo08uS904Rg.summary: A short How to ADHD explainer, featuring Brendan Mahan, on why simple tasks can feel impossible for people with ADHD. It introduces the 'wall of awful', a pile of past failures, shame and anxiety that builds up in front of a task and blocks starting it.
Uo08uS904Rg.why: HN commenters use it as the go-to name and explanation for task paralysis and procrastination, and say it helped them see why they avoid tasks.

U4FNBMZsqrY.summary: Mick Gordon's GDC 2017 session on composing the Doom (2016) soundtrack. He details his compositional process, production techniques and the experimental instrument and synth design behind the music.
U4FNBMZsqrY.why: HN raves about it as one of the best conference talks, showing a master's creative process and sound design.

UJ7Qc3bsxjI.summary: Geologist Nick Zentner of Central Washington University gives an hour-long public lecture on the great earthquakes of the Pacific Northwest, including the Cascadia subduction zone and the evidence for past megaquakes. It is part of his Downtown Geology Lecture Series, recorded in Ellensburg in 2016.
UJ7Qc3bsxjI.why: HN commenters offer it as a dry but fascinating, hype-free introduction to Cascadia earthquake risk and the evidence for past events.

UEAMfLPZZhE.summary: The first lecture in Martin Kleppmann's 8-lecture distributed systems series from the University of Cambridge undergraduate course. It introduces the subject, and accompanying lecture notes are available.
UEAMfLPZZhE.why: HN regularly recommends the series as a free, accessible, theory-oriented course on distributed computing that complements his book Designing Data-Intensive Applications.

U2huVf1l4UE.summary: Chess player John Bartholomew plays opponents rated below 1000 on Chess.com and comments on optimal strategy and typical mistakes at that level. It is part of his Climbing the Rating Ladder series.
U2huVf1l4UE.why: Strongly recommended as a way to improve at chess, since it explains the basics and common mistakes at each rating level.

URSWYvyc42M.summary: Sandi Metz's RailsConf 2013 talk offers practical guidelines for deciding what to test and how, so tests stay cheap and stable. She argues for testing the public interface rather than implementation and using mocks appropriately.
URSWYvyc42M.why: HN recommends it as an incredible talk whose testing principles apply beyond Ruby.

UcN7SGGoCNI.summary: Vegan advocate Erin Janus explains the dairy industry in about five minutes, covering how milk is produced and the treatment of cows and calves. It is an advocacy piece and includes graphic material.
UcN7SGGoCNI.why: HN commenters in veganism and food threads link it as a short, info-dense explanation that some say opened their eyes, though others dispute it.

UjZYMI1zB9s.summary: Valve's feature-length documentary following three professional gamers competing in the first Dota 2 International tournament for a million dollar prize. It shows the sacrifices and pressures of top-level esports.
UjZYMI1zB9s.why: HN recommends it as an engaging look at the life of pro Dota players and the early rise of esports, though one commenter notes it is somewhat promotional.

UBc7qBS1Ujo.summary: Shaun's roughly 2.7-hour video essay on The Bell Curve. It covers intelligence, the g factor, IQ tests, IQ versus environment and the politics behind the book, with a critical reading of the sources.
UBc7qBS1Ujo.why: HN commenters most often cite it as a thorough, well-sourced debunking of The Bell Curve and of popular IQ claims.

UawS3_iuHoA.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's DEF CON 19 talk on the weaknesses of SSL and the certificate authority system. He explains how CA trust became a problem and proposes an alternative that removes the CA oligopoly without reducing security.
UawS3_iuHoA.why: HN points to it as the classic overview of why TLS certificate trust is flawed, and it resurfaces whenever CA or HTTPS security comes up.

Uwl3-jBNEd4.summary: Ben Felix explains how to compare renting and buying a home by looking at unrecoverable costs, and distills it into the 5% rule of thumb. It is framed for a Canadian audience but broadly applicable.
Uwl3-jBNEd4.why: HN points to it for a clean first-order framework for the rent versus buy decision.

UEfP1OKKz_Q.summary: Tom Scott explains the design of the British BS 1363 plug and socket, including fuses, shutters and safety features, and why he thinks it beats other plugs.
UEfP1OKKz_Q.why: HN treats it as the obligatory video to share whenever plugs and sockets come up, praised for its safety reasoning.

URJ_qSXruW0.summary: SsethTzeentach reviews Space Station 13, the chaotic multiplayer game, by recounting absurd stories of singularities, malfunctioning AIs and plasma fires.
URJ_qSXruW0.why: HN considers it the go-to link for conveying the chaos of Space Station 13 in any related discussion.

UnU7DJXiMAQ.summary: Pannenkoek explains how Super Mario 64 handles wall, floor and ceiling collisions, including triangles, normal vectors, quarter steps and out of bounds. It is a detailed 37-minute technical walkthrough of the game's physics.
UnU7DJXiMAQ.why: Praised as an engrossing, in-depth look at SM64 mechanics that is surprisingly compelling to watch.

UANN2Eu6ZnM.summary: Raymond Hettinger's PyBay 2019 talk on the mental habits behind effective programming, drawn from coaching, teaching and StackOverflow. He covers problem decomposition, chunking, managing working memory and getting unstuck.
UANN2Eu6ZnM.why: HN recommends it as a Python talk with lessons that apply to any programming, especially chunking to manage complexity.

UIKGV2cTgqA.summary: An amateur animation of Tom Lehrer's satirical song New Math, which pokes fun at 1960s math teaching and subtraction in base 8. The animation illustrates the old and new subtraction methods.
UIKGV2cTgqA.why: HN brings it up whenever curriculum fads or Common Core complaints appear, as a funny precedent from the 1960s.

UV1V9-nnaAs.summary: A roughly 45-minute vintage US military instructional film that gives a comprehensive overview of celestial navigation, covering sextant use and the theory behind lines of position.
UV1V9-nnaAs.why: HN points to it as an unusually clear teaching film on how celestial navigation works, and as an example of how good old military training material is.

Uj6skZIxPuI.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews ancient-DNA geneticist David Reich about human prehistory, including the small group that left Africa around 70,000 years ago and the Yamnaya expansion.
Uj6skZIxPuI.why: Recommended as a nuanced, up-to-date account of human prehistory from a leading researcher in ancient DNA.

UnURElCzGc0.summary: A segment from Carl Sagan's original Cosmos explaining the fourth spatial dimension through analogy with a two-dimensional world and shadow projection.
UnURElCzGc0.why: HN recommends it as the clearest intuitive introduction to thinking about a fourth dimension.

Uooh0Y9fC_M.summary: John Carmack's roughly three-hour QuakeCon 2013 keynote, delivered from a few bullet points. Topics include his Haskell experiments with functional programming and static typing, game state, and cloud gaming.
Uooh0Y9fC_M.why: Recommended to Carmack fans as the keynote with his functional programming adventures and for his fluent, wide-ranging talk.

UyyjU8fzEYU.summary: Neuroscientist Jill Bolte Taylor describes watching her own brain functions shut down during a massive stroke. She gives a first-person account of losing speech, motion and self-awareness.
UyyjU8fzEYU.why: Recommended as a vivid first-person view of the right hemisphere in control, often linked to meditation and non-dual experience.

UE-k4hYHIDE.summary: Cathode Ray Dude's hour-long retrospective on the ABIT BP6, the dual-Celeron motherboard. He covers early multiprocessing, its legend, a build, running NT 4, benchmarks and the pros and cons of early SMP.
UE-k4hYHIDE.why: HN recommends it as an excellent history of the famous ABIT BP6 board.

UGhfB-NICzg.summary: A 1991 NeXT promotional video that stages a head-to-head programming contest between a NeXT computer and a Sun workstation. It shows NeXT's interface builder and object-oriented tooling producing an application far faster than traditional UNIX development.
UGhfB-NICzg.why: HN uses it as the canonical example of rapid application development and object-oriented tooling productivity, though many note it is biased marketing.

UWEjxkkB8Xs.summary: An Every Frame a Painting video essay on Buster Keaton's visual comedy, examining how he built and framed his gags. It uses clips from his silent films to show the thinking behind them.
UWEjxkkB8Xs.why: Recommended as a short, excellent analysis of Keaton and visual comedy.

UWvRorX0KhQ.summary: A three-minute clip of magician Ricky Jay performing a card manipulation routine, including table faro shuffles. The routine builds in intensity and ends with a surprising finish.
UWvRorX0KhQ.why: HN people share it as a classic example of sleight-of-hand mastery whose ending is mind-blowing.

U_X5uR7VC4M.summary: An episode of the comedic You Suck at Photoshop series in which Donnie Hoyle teaches distort, warp and layer effects while vandalizing a Vanagon in the image. It won Webby awards as a how-to and comedy series.
U_X5uR7VC4M.why: Recommended as a classic, funny Photoshop tutorial series with a strong comedic personality.

Ucp0TTmvqOE.summary: Tesla's roughly four-hour Autonomy Day investor event covers its in-house self-driving chip, vision-only approach, fleet data engine and robotaxi plans, with talks by Andrej Karpathy and others.
Ucp0TTmvqOE.why: Cited both as a primary source on Tesla's technical autonomy approach and, later, for Musk's unmet robotaxi predictions.

UiS27feX8o0.summary: Technology Connections examines an old feature-rich microwave and shows how it uses a humidity or steam sensor and lookup data to cook food well, arguing it beats many modern ones.
UiS27feX8o0.why: Cited again and again in microwave and smart-appliance threads as proof that older appliances were smarter, especially for steam-sensor cooking.

UjtOGPJ0URM.summary: A short Kurzgesagt animation explaining the Great Filter, the idea that finding alien life might be bad news because it implies something usually destroys civilizations. It connects the concept to the Fermi paradox.
UjtOGPJ0URM.why: HN links it as a concise, accessible explainer whenever the Fermi paradox or Great Filter comes up, though one commenter criticized its lack of source attribution.

UmKf8smvGsA.summary: Aging Wheels tests how towing trailers affects the range of electric trucks, including a Silverado EV. It shows that trailer aerodynamics matters far more than added weight.
UmKf8smvGsA.why: HN cites it as data-backed evidence that weight has little effect on EV range while air resistance from trailers does.

Uv1UfLPK7_Q.summary: Joe Armstrong, creator of Erlang, and Jeremy Ruston, creator of TiddlyWiki, discuss hypertext, Ted Nelson's idea of intertwingled knowledge, and a way to combine TiddlyWiki with Erlang. It is a Code Mesh LDN 2018 talk.
Uv1UfLPK7_Q.why: Recommended in note-taking and personal wiki threads for its enthusiasm about granular, densely linked notes and TiddlyWiki.

U6qZPx4uD0g.summary: Dave Jones builds the Evil Mad Scientist discrete-component 555 timer kit, then tests it and explains the internal circuitry of the 555 at transistor level. He finishes with scope waveforms.
U6qZPx4uD0g.why: Recommended as a deep, hands-on explanation of how a 555 timer works inside.

UDtlvZGmHYk.summary: A BBC Earth clip from The Hunt showing Portia jumping spiders, which leap many times their body length and ambush prey larger than themselves.
UDtlvZGmHYk.why: HN recommends it as striking footage of how cleverly jumping spiders plan their attacks.

UN8bJb8biZU.summary: John Oliver explains SLAPP suits, lawsuits designed to silence critics through legal costs, after his show's legal fight with coal executive Bob Murray. It covers how such suits work and why state anti-SLAPP laws matter.
UN8bJb8biZU.why: HN recommends it whenever legal threats against critics or open-source authors come up, often as the best accessible primer on SLAPP suits.

UOHURuAf5iY.summary: Practical Engineering gives a short introduction to concrete, covering the difference between concrete and cement, the ingredients, and reinforcement. It includes a hydraulic press demonstration of compressive strength.
UOHURuAf5iY.why: Commenters link it as an approachable explanation of concrete basics in threads about Roman concrete, construction and sand supply.

UQuIVsNzqDk.summary: Corridor Crew tracks down Disney's lost sodium vapor prism process, used for Mary Poppins-era transparency mattes. They explain how a narrow sodium wavelength and a beam splitter enabled better compositing than green screen.
UQuIVsNzqDk.why: Recommended as a fun, informative rediscovery of a lost film-effects technique.

UmIgNfp-MdI.summary: A short concept video of Microsoft's unreleased Courier, a dual-screen tablet designed as a digital notebook with clippings and annotation. It was first leaked by Gizmodo in 2009.
UmIgNfp-MdI.why: HN treats it as a gold-standard concept demo and a what-might-have-been for dual-screen and digital notebook devices.

UyFF4cpMVag.summary: Short footage of the 1983 Soyuz T-10-1 pad fire, in which the launch escape tower pulled the crew away seconds before the rocket exploded.
UyFF4cpMVag.why: HN cites it as the one dramatic real-world proof that a launch escape system works.

UAeJHAFjwPM.summary: Veritasium visits the US Navy's Crane facility to test top night vision goggles. It explains how image intensifier tubes and thermal or digital systems work and compares the generations of the technology.
UAeJHAFjwPM.why: Commenters point to it as a clear explanation of the different types of night vision and why analog image intensifiers behave differently from digital ones.

UBX2QQHlQ_I.summary: Matt Parker's stand-up routine about spreadsheets, taken from the Festival of the Spoken Nerd DVD Full Frontal Nerdity. It features Excel used in unexpected ways, including turning an image into a spreadsheet.
UBX2QQHlQ_I.why: HN recommends it as a funny piece on Excel used in ways it shouldn't be.

UC_BCz0pzMw.summary: Real Engineering looks at why nuclear power plants are expensive and how their economics compare with fossil and renewable alternatives. It is based on a video from the Illinois Energy Professors.
UC_BCz0pzMw.why: Recommended as a clear walkthrough of nuclear plant economics and why incentives favor other generation.

UIDb6VBO9os.summary: A dotJS 2012 conference talk by Fat (of Twitter Bootstrap fame) on what open source really means and why maintainers feel guilty about it. It covers the obligations, expectations and burnout that come with releasing popular open source software, delivered with humor.
UIDb6VBO9os.why: HN commenters cite it as a funny and candid first-hand account of the guilt and burnout of a prolific open source developer.

UX4KklvCDmg.summary: Wendover Productions explains why American towns, retail and buildings increasingly look alike, covering zoning pressures, corporate standardization and cheap construction types like 5-over-1 buildings.
UX4KklvCDmg.why: HN uses it as a good explanation of how US zoning and economics produce sameness.

Ufmu1WD2TSk.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation on South Korea's record-low fertility rate and rapidly aging population. It explains why a demographic collapse looks hard to reverse and projects the population shrinking sharply by 2060.
Ufmu1WD2TSk.why: Go-to link for the consequences of collapsing birth rates, showing why South Korea's decline looks unfixable.

Um63OQz3bjo.summary: A two-minute animated introduction to Bitcoin from 2011, explaining it as a peer-to-peer digital currency. It was widely shared in Bitcoin's early days as the standard newcomer explainer.
Um63OQz3bjo.why: HN commenters sent it to newcomers as a short, simple first explanation of Bitcoin.

Uwuv05aZ6ug.summary: Raymond Hettinger's PyBay 2019 talk on the mental strategies he uses when programming in Python, such as chunking, solving a simpler related problem, and repeating tasks manually until patterns emerge. This version is re-synced with the slides.
Uwuv05aZ6ug.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining talk on how working memory shapes code and how to reduce cognitive load.

UziFw-jQSks.summary: Atrocity Guide covers the 1965 dolphin experiments of Dr. John C. Lilly and Margaret Howe, who tried to teach dolphins English. It traces the bizarre methods and Lilly's later drug-fueled beliefs.
UziFw-jQSks.why: HN recommends it as a decent, entertaining summary of Lilly's life and work whenever dolphin communication research comes up.

UHbQmqmmIFk.summary: A one-minute archive video of the 2Advanced Studios v2 website from 2001, a showcase of the elaborate futuristic Flash interfaces the agency was known for.
UHbQmqmmIFk.why: HN points to it as the example of the weird, artistic, animation-heavy web UIs of the Flash era.

UKxQTvqcpSg.summary: PBS Space Time explores whether time causes gravity, explaining that gravity does not truly warp the flow of time but arises from time gradients. It revisits how gravitational time dilation works in general relativity.
UKxQTvqcpSg.why: Recommended as a good explanation of what happens when gravity acts on an object.

Uo3cL4nrGOk.summary: A comedy sketch by Kai Lentit in which a senior JavaScript developer is interviewed, parodying the chaos of the JavaScript ecosystem.
Uo3cL4nrGOk.why: Shared as a joke about JavaScript culture and tooling, usually without much explanation.

U03XXzcThGU.summary: Brian Bucklew of Freehold Games discusses design decisions behind Caves of Qud and Sproggiwood at IRDC 2015. The talk centers on data-driven, event-driven engine design.
U03XXzcThGU.why: HN points to it for insight into how the Caves of Qud developer thinks about game engines.

U3EEmVfbKNs.summary: Destin of Smarter Every Day goes behind the scenes at the 23andMe lab to show how genotyping works. He also discusses DNA testing and privacy.
U3EEmVfbKNs.why: Pointed to as an interesting look inside how consumer DNA testing companies process samples.

U5kIdtMJGc8.summary: A TED interview in which Chris Anderson talks with Jim Simons about his life: code-breaking, math, founding Renaissance Technologies, and his philanthropy in math education and origins-of-life research.
U5kIdtMJGc8.why: HN cites it as a view of Simons as a humble, pragmatic person, with the caveat that the host's questions are weak.

U6xJfP7-HCc.summary: Numberphile's James Grime makes the case for base 12 (dozenal) over base 10, showing how twelve's many divisors make arithmetic and everyday fractions easier.
U6xJfP7-HCc.why: HN uses it as the accessible overview of the dozenal system whenever base 12 or the 12 times table comes up.

U88jj6PSD7w.summary: A two-minute Big Think clip of Slavoj Zizek arguing that happiness is a conformist, even unethical goal. He asks why one would want to be happy when one could be interesting.
U88jj6PSD7w.why: HN shares it as a short, provocative counterpoint in threads on purpose, goals and the pursuit of happiness.

UBVV8pch1dM.summary: A Veritasium explainer on how the brain works and how we learn. It is inspired by Kahneman's Thinking, Fast and Slow and covers System 1 and System 2 thinking and why harder learning builds skill.
UBVV8pch1dM.why: HN uses it as a short, clear summary of the fast and slow thinking idea.

UGttmR2DTY8.summary: Casey Neistat's social experiment in New York City where he tries to 'steal' his own bike with various tools, showing how little stops passers-by from helping.
UGttmR2DTY8.why: HN cites it as a demonstration of how easily bikes get stolen in public.

UQB4W8C0rZI.summary: Pierre Sprey, a designer of the F-16 and A-10, explains why he thinks the F-35 will not hold up on the modern battlefield. It is part one of a series of F-35 critique videos.
UQB4W8C0rZI.why: HN cites it as an insider's critique of the F-35 whenever the program's problems come up.

URvWSsAgtJE.summary: A man spends six months and $1500 making a chicken sandwich entirely from scratch: growing vegetables, making salt from seawater, milking a cow for cheese, grinding wheat, collecting honey and killing a chicken.
URvWSsAgtJE.why: Used as a go-to example of how much hidden effort and infrastructure lies behind simple everyday things.

USHvvSbYmJA.summary: LGR reviews the weeCee, a tiny mini PC that boots MS-DOS and Windows from a microSD card. It offers Sound Blaster Pro and General MIDI compatibility with VGA output, and the video tries it with DOS and Windows 98 games.
USHvvSbYmJA.why: Cited as an example of a compact, ready-made way to play retro DOS games on real hardware without collecting old machines.

UTqZNujQOlA.summary: Jonathan Blow demos his prototype programming language, covering the base language and compile-time execution, including running a game while compiling. The video is about 70 minutes of demo followed by Q&A.
UTqZNujQOlA.why: HN cites it as an early demonstration of compile-time code execution, predating its popularity in languages like Zig.

UWacQrEcMHk.summary: Blender Guru's Andrew Price proposes a redesign of Blender's user interface, answering the usability problems raised in earlier parts of the series. He later noted the proposal had flaws and posted a follow-up.
UWacQrEcMHk.why: Seen as an inflection point in how Blender's UI was perceived, and as helping kick off the 2.8 redesign.

UXZGCwAJpbM.summary: Digital Foundry investigates why Resident Evil Village on PC runs worse with Capcom's Denuvo DRM than a cracked version. They benchmark and confirm performance and frame-pacing differences.
UXZGCwAJpbM.why: Cited as the evidence that Denuvo DRM measurably hurts game performance.

UacbJ72dluU.summary: Robert Scoble interviews Paul Graham at Y Combinator's Mountain View headquarters as 36 new startups debut. They discuss what YC is, and Graham's no-assholes rule.
UacbJ72dluU.why: Linked as a source for Paul Graham's no-assholes rule and his comments on early YC funding.

Ufp8weYYDE8.summary: Insider explains how The Mandalorian replaced green screens with LED walls that project real-time 3D environments behind actors, with over half the show filmed on such virtual sets.
Ufp8weYYDE8.why: Cited as an explanation of LED virtual production and how it solves green-screen lighting problems.

Ug8NH67_EfE.summary: Rick Falkvinge responds to viewer feedback on his earlier Lightning Network video and raises a flaw he says was not previously discussed. The main thread is the network's unsolved routing problem.
Ug8NH67_EfE.why: HN commenters cite it, with a pointer to the section from about 10:00, when arguing that Lightning has no solved routing algorithm; most mentions are critical of Lightning.

UlJku_CSyNg.summary: A 1994 Today Show clip in which hosts puzzle over what the Internet is and how to say the at-sign in email addresses. It is a short archival piece from the early days of the web.
UlJku_CSyNg.why: Used as a stock example of mainstream bafflement at new technology, often invoked in crypto debates.

UphN1_7nP8U.summary: A short side-by-side demo of a large image loading over a slow connection in JPEG, progressive mozjpeg, JPEG XL and AVIF. It shows how each codec renders partial data.
UphN1_7nP8U.why: HN uses it as visual evidence that JPEG XL decodes progressively while AVIF shows nothing until fully loaded.

UwerBZG83YM.summary: Former CIA officer Frank Snepp describes how, working in Vietnam from 1969 to 1975, he planted stories in major newspapers to support Agency goals. He notes that some younger reporters refused to take the bait.
UwerBZG83YM.why: Cited as a first-hand account of how intelligence agencies have placed stories in the press.

U3Ak-SmyHHQ.summary: A scene from It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia in which Mac argues against evolution, claiming science is a liar sometimes. It is a short comedic courtroom clip.
U3Ak-SmyHHQ.why: Used as a joke whenever someone dismisses scientific consensus.

U7s5pT3Rris.summary: A short clip of John McCain, asked about Iran, singing 'Bomb bomb bomb, bomb bomb Iran' to the tune of the Beach Boys' Barbara Ann.
U7s5pT3Rris.why: HN brings it up in Iran-related threads as a critical or darkly joking reminder of casual hawkish rhetoric.

UDfAdHBtK_Q.summary: The Who performing Won't Get Fooled Again at Shepperton Studios in 1978, filmed for The Kids Are Alright. It was Keith Moon's last performance with the band.
UDfAdHBtK_Q.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke, quoting the lyric about the new boss being the same as the old boss.

UEIn8GJIg0E.summary: A short clip of Meskel Square in Addis Ababa, a busy crossroads where vehicles and pedestrians mix with few apparent rules. Filmed in 2013.
UEIn8GJIg0E.why: Cited in debates on removing traffic signals as an example of chaotic, rule-light traffic, with some saying it does not work.

UFcb-XF1RPQ.summary: A short scene from the film Pirates of Silicon Valley where Steve Jobs confronts Bill Gates after the Macintosh announcement over Windows copying Apple's work, and Gates replies that it doesn't matter.
UFcb-XF1RPQ.why: HN quotes the scene when a better product loses to a more pragmatic or dominant competitor.

UOWexFaRylM.summary: A DEF CON 22 panel with Rob Graham, Paul McMillan and Dan Tentler on the quirks of scanning the entire internet with masscan. They discuss how fast IPv4 can be scanned and what the results reveal.
UOWexFaRylM.why: HN cites it as evidence that scanning the whole IPv4 address space is trivial and takes only minutes to hours.

UOYi4NzxlhE.summary: A clip from the 2011 film Margin Call in which an analyst explains to the firm's executive the dire state of their investment firm at the onset of the 2008 financial crisis.
UOYi4NzxlhE.why: Cited as a reference scene when commenters see signs of impending economic or institutional trouble.

UP1YsMlrfF0.summary: A short 2013 video in which Roger Ver says Mt. Gox's withdrawal delays are not caused by a lack of liquidity. Mt. Gox collapsed months later, and the description carries a later update and apology.
UP1YsMlrfF0.why: Cited critically as an example of someone vouching for Mt. Gox just before its collapse.

USKD3vPD6ZA.summary: Michael Reeves rigs up a camera and software that tracks a goldfish's movements to choose stock trades, tied to wallstreetbets sentiment. It is a comedic programming and electronics stunt.
USKD3vPD6ZA.why: Mostly invoked as a joke in threads about monkeys or darts beating professional stock pickers, and about loose definitions of AI.

UTduy7Qkvk8.summary: A clip from Eddie Izzard's Dress to Kill about having a flag as justification for claiming a land.
UTduy7Qkvk8.why: Invoked as a joke in threads about ownership and entitlement.

UXA--dj2-CY.summary: A short clip of Joe Biden speaking about leveraging loan guarantees to get Ukraine's prosecutor general fired, with a partisan description framing it as corruption.
UXA--dj2-CY.why: Used almost entirely as a critical, politically charged citation in unrelated threads, not as something recommended.

UY9P0QSxlnI.summary: An animated map showing the borders and populations of European countries for every year since 400 BC. Vassal states and colonies are excluded from population counts.
UY9P0QSxlnI.why: HN users link it whenever a thread needs a quick illustration of how much European borders have shifted and how much conflict there was.

UYHFrf5ci_g.summary: A 2017 video arguing that banks and Blockstream steered Bitcoin toward the Lightning Network. It is partisan commentary from the Bitcoin Cash side of the scaling dispute.
UYHFrf5ci_g.why: HN mentions are thin and mostly cite it in Lightning Network discussions, as a reference point for that critical viewpoint rather than a recommendation.

UZ1XLqc5IUg.summary: A driver tests Tesla Model S Autopilot firmware 17.7.2 on hardware 2.0 and records numerous failures, including crossing to the wrong side of the road.
UZ1XLqc5IUg.why: Cited critically as evidence that early Autopilot 2 was unsafe and overpromised.

UZ9qcp6Lcno.summary: A 1999 Qwest commercial in which a weary traveler at a remote motel is told every room offers every movie ever made, on demand. It was shot at Roy's Motel in Amboy, California.
UZ9qcp6Lcno.why: HN brings it up as an eerily prescient ad that foresaw on-demand streaming years before YouTube or Netflix.

U_o8gerare0.summary: A 1993 episode of The Computer Chronicles on the early Internet, with guests including Howard Rheingold discussing online community. It is a window into how the internet was seen and what hardware was in use at the time.
U_o8gerare0.why: Cited as period footage for how people thought about the early internet and 90s computing.

Ug75diEyiA0.summary: A one-minute clip of the famous 'Where's the Beef?' catchphrase from a classic fast food commercial.
Ug75diEyiA0.why: Used purely as a joke when a thread involves beef, the name Beef, or a lack of substance.

UiOzGI4MqSU.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs saying Microsoft has no taste, from an interview about Windows. It is an excerpt reposted by a fan channel.
UiOzGI4MqSU.why: Cited in debates about Windows design quality, sometimes agreeing and sometimes disputing the claim.

UlCYFh8U2xM.summary: A short news clip of WHO official Bruce Aylward's 2020 interview with a Hong Kong outlet, in which he stalls and then ends the call when asked about Taiwan's WHO membership. He also says he would want to be treated in China if infected.
UlCYFh8U2xM.why: Cited, almost always critically, as evidence of Chinese influence over the WHO during the Covid pandemic.

UnJ3amzJM94.summary: A 2019 Android Dev Summit session on the scoped storage model in Android 10. It gives a plan overview and best practices for apps adapting to the new restrictions.
UnJ3amzJM94.why: Cited as the official explanation of Google's scoped storage changes and its intent to limit broad file access.

UqBmdZ-BNig.summary: A one-minute clip from Cambridge's Prof. Holger Babinsky that debunks the equal transit time explanation of lift. It shows how air actually flows over a wing.
UqBmdZ-BNig.why: Linked in lift-theory arguments as a clear demonstration that air over the top of a wing does not need to catch up with air underneath.

UuLaxbFKAcc.summary: Totally Gridbag is a short humorous animation about the frustrations of Java Swing's GridBagLayout, originally made as a Flash cartoon.
UuLaxbFKAcc.why: It is posted as an in-joke whenever Java GUI layout, Swing or desktop UI toolkits come up.

UwLjK9LFpeo.summary: A one-minute clip of Stephen Colbert at the White House Correspondents' Dinner delivering the line that reality has a well-known liberal bias.
UwLjK9LFpeo.why: HN uses it to credit the origin of the quip when someone repeats it, sometimes as a joke.
